posts.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
posts.summary: In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right. Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like…
bullets: The rapid expansion of AI data centers is driving a significant resurgence in natural-gas power generation, as utilities struggle to meet surging electricity demand.
In the PJM grid region, natural-gas projects now account for nearly half of the 200 gigawatts of capacity currently in the interconnection queue.
Energy modelers estimate that if all pending projects in the PJM queue are completed, the grid's reliance on fossil fuels would increase from 61% to 67%.
Tech hyperscalers are increasingly exploring off-grid natural-gas power plants to bypass grid constraints, contributing to a 45% year-over-year increase in Meta's greenhouse gas emissions.

posts.title: Li Auto beats Q3 revenue guidance as net loss narrows, expects Q4 return to profit
posts.summary:
Third-quarter revenue rose 5.4% year-on-year to $4.29 billion, while net loss narrowed 81.8% sequentially.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto reported Q3 revenue of $4.29 billion, exceeding the upper end of its guidance, while net loss narrowed significantly by 81.8% sequentially to 309.7 million yuan.
Profitability improved as the overall gross margin rose to 16.7%, supported by a rebound in vehicle margins to 15.3% following the launch of updated flagship models.
The company achieved positive free cash flow of 2.0 billion yuan in Q3 and projects a return to profitability in the fourth quarter with delivery targets of 110,000 to 115,000 vehicles.

posts.title: China passenger NEV retail sales fall 13% year-on-year in November 1-22, penetration reaches 71.3%
posts.summary:
China's passenger NEVs recorded retail sales of 702,000 units from November 1 to 22, down 13% from a year earlier but up 7% from the same period last month.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's passenger NEV retail sales reached 702,000 units from November 1 to 22, representing a 13% year-on-year decline but a 7% increase compared to the previous month.
NEV market penetration hit 71.3% for retail and 76.6% for wholesale during the period, highlighting the continued dominance of electric vehicles over internal combustion engines.
Total passenger vehicle retail sales in China fell 25% year-on-year to 984,000 units, indicating a broader market contraction that is being partially offset by the high NEV adoption rate.

posts.title: Nio goes all-in on AI at 12th anniversary tech day, sees over $1.2 trillion in auto AI value
posts.summary:
Nio launched new AI-powered smart driving and cabin systems and aims to manage over $52 billion in battery assets by 2030.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio launched its Nio World Model (NWM) 3.0, which utilizes 4D spatiotemporal compression to reduce onboard computing resource requirements by 36-fold.
The company claims the new model reduces driver interventions by 40% and improves control latency by over 50% through vehicle-level joint optimization of algorithms and hardware.

CEO William Li estimates that AI integration could unlock over $1.2 trillion in new commercial value for the global automotive industry, positioning Nio to leverage AI across its energy and smart driving ecosystems.

posts.title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Nov. 25
posts.summary:
Hybrid-bonded 3D NAND analog IMC; defect-aware chiplet matching for HI yield; HBF latency reduction for GPU systems; backside clock meshes for BSPDN; LLM-agent verification for post-quantum HW; self-supervised CMP virtual metrology; e-beam stitching losses in SOI waveguides.
The post Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Nov. 25 appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: IBM and Micron have developed a hybrid-bonded 3D-NAND analog in-memory compute macro that achieves a high density of 4.8 million weights per square millimeter.
New research from Georgia Tech and Nvidia introduces 'SlipStream,' a method to mitigate latency and SRAM overheads in GPU systems utilizing heterogeneous buffer fabrics.
KAIST researchers are exploring backside clock mesh architectures for Backside Power Delivery Networks (BSPDN), a critical area for scaling future high-performance logic.
A collaborative study involving Ampere Computing proposes 'DT-MATCH,' a methodology that optimizes heterogeneous integration yields by accounting for both defect patterns and chiplet topology.
The roundup highlights advancements in post-quantum cryptographic hardware verification using LLM agents, addressing security gaps that traditional testing and manual reviews often overlook.
